To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the opposition to the wind power project in the study area was mainly driven by a landscape commons.
landscape commons are not necessarily a shared resource and that the landscape is not a neutral resource for wind power development.

the emergence and structuring process of an opponent network to a highly controversial wind power project in France was based on the shared landscape resources of the project area and the mobilization of a specific set of landscape values, which were used by opponents as a tool to oppose the project.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How does a wind power project, and the opposition to it, emerge?
the following questions : What are the landscape resources mobilized and the stakes of the opposition to wind power?
a specific form of social movement, namely the landscape commons, that is, the mobilization of the landscape as a common resource in the face of wind power projects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the opponents of the wind farm project are not a homogeneous group of people.
the wind power project has not only been a trigger of the emergence of a network of opponents, but also that the project itself has been the outcome of the development of this network.
landscape resources are a major factor of the structuration of the opponent network, but they are not the only one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

landscape commons is a useful concept in order to understand the emergence of a network of opposition to wind turbines, as it allows for an analysis of the social and material dimensions of this opposition.
we have shown the importance of landscape resources for the emergence and structuring process of a networked opposition to a wind power project.
landscape commons are a resource for opposition to wind power development.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the emergence of this network is the result of the interaction of several factors: the landscape resources involved in the project (the wind power fault lines) and their appropriation by the different actors, the nature of the actors’ mobilization, the nature of their relationships and their capacity to mobilize resources.
, in the context of wind power, the “landscape” is not only a matter of aesthetics or a matter of “nature”.
the emergence of this opponent network is not the result of the mobilisation of a pre-existent community of interests.
